questions.question: Ravi can row a boat in still water at the speed of 14 km/h. If a river is flowing at the sped of 2 km/h and Ravi takes 3 hours to cover a certain distance upstream, then how much time will he take to cover the same distance downstream?
questions.solution:
Given:

Speed of the boat = 14kmph 

Flow of the river = 2 kmph

Ravi takes 3 hours to cover a certain distance upstream

Concept used:

Distance = Time × Speed

While going upstream, the speed of a boat and the flow of the river get added to calculate the effective speed. On the other hand, while going downstream, to take the effective speed, the difference between the speed of the boat and the flow of the river is considered. 

Calculation:

Effective speed during the upstream journey = (14 - 2) kmph = 12kmph

Distance covered = 12 × 3 = 36 hours

Effective speed during the downstream journey = (14 + 2) kmph = 16kmph

So, time taken by Ravi to cover 36 km downstream = 36 ÷ 16 = 2.25 hours = 2 hours 15 minutes

**∴ Ravi will take 2 hours 15 minutes to cover the same distance downstream.**

questions.question: Geeta can assemble a toy in 10 minutes, whereas Sudha can assemble the same toy in 15 minutes. If they work together, how much time will they take to assemble 60 toys?
questions.solution:
Given:

Geeta can assemble a toy in 10 minutes.

Sudha can assemble the same toy in 15 minutes.

Concept used:

Entire work = Work done in each minute × Time taken (in minutes)

Calculation:

LCM (10,15) = 30

Let the entire work (making a toy) be the LCM of the time taken by Geeta & Sudha.

So, the entire work = 30 units

Geeta does in a minute = 30 ÷ 10 = 3 units of work

Sudha does in a minute = 30 ÷ 15 = 2 units of work

Time taken to finish the entire work together = 30 ÷ (3 + 2) = 6 minutes 

So, time taken to make 60 toys together = 6 × 60 = 360 minutes = 6 hours

**∴ If they work together, they will take 6 hours to assemble 60 toys.**

questions.question:
Simplify the following expression.

(2a - b - 3c)(4a² + b² + 9c² + 2ab + 6ac - 3bc)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the standard **algebraic identity**: (x + y + z)(x² + y² + z² − xy − yz − zx) = x³ + y³ + z³ − 3xyz.

Identify the terms: x = 2a, y = −b, and z = −3c.

Substitute into the result: (2a)³ + (−b)³ + (−3c)³ − 3(2a)(−b)(−3c).

Simplified result: 8a³ − b³ − 27c³ − 18abc.

**∴ The correct answer is 8a³ − b³ − 27c³ − 18abc.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The expression is (2a − b − 3c)(4a² + b² + 9c² + 2ab + 6ac − 3bc).

**Formula Used:** (x + y + z)(x² + y² + z² − xy − yz − zx) = x³ + y³ + z³ − 3xyz.

⇒ Let x = 2a, y = −b, and z = −3c.

⇒ Check the second bracket terms:

⇒ x² = (2a)² = 4a², y² = (−b)² = b², z² = (−3c)² = 9c².

⇒ −xy = −(2a)(−b) = 2ab, −yz = −(−b)(−3c) = −3bc, −zx = −(−3c)(2a) = 6ac.

⇒ The given expression perfectly matches the **identity expansion**.

⇒ Result = (2a)³ + (−b)³ + (−3c)³ − 3(2a)(−b)(−3c)

⇒ Result = 8a³ − b³ − 27c³ − 18abc.

**∴ The correct answer is 8a³ − b³ − 27c³ − 18abc.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Cubes Identity

The expression x³ + y³ + z³ − 3xyz is equal to (x + y + z)(x² + y² + z² − xy − yz − zx).

Special Case (Conditional Identity)

If the sum of variables x + y + z = 0, then the sum of their cubes x³ + y³ + z³ is exactly equal to 3xyz.

Square of a Trinomial

The square of three terms is given by (x + y + z)² = x² + y² + z² + 2xy + 2yz + 2zx.</p

questions.question: A reduction of 20% in the rate of sugar enables Sudhir to get 6 kg more sugar for Rs. 960. What is the reduced rate of sugar per kg?
questions.solution:
Given:

20% reduction results to 6 kg more sugar.

Concept used:

Application of percentage

Calculation:

Let the previous price of the sugar be Rs. P for the certain amount R kg.

Now, previously (R + 6) kg could have been acquired at = 960 ÷ 0.8 = Rs. 1200

So, Rs. (1200 - 960) = Rs. 240 results to 6 kg.

Hence, previous price of sugar = 240 ÷ 6 = Rs. 40 per kg

So, at Rs. 960, One could get = 960 ÷ 40 = 24kg sugar

Now, recent price of sugar = 960 ÷ (24 + 6) = Rs. 32

**∴ The reduced rate of sugar is Rs. 32 per kg.**

questions.question: If cosec² θ (cos θ - 1)(1 + cos θ) = k, then what is the value of k?
questions.solution:
Given:

cosec2 θ (cos θ - 1)(1 + cos θ) = k

Concept used:

Cosec α = 1/Sin α

Sin² α + Cos² α = 1

(a + b)(a - b) = a² - b² 

Calculation:

cosec2 θ (cos θ - 1)(1 + cos θ) = k

⇒ cosec2 θ (1 - cos θ)(1 + cos θ) = -k

⇒ cosec2 θ (1 - cos² θ) = -k

⇒ cosec2 θ × sin² θ = -k

⇒ 1 = -k

⇒ k = -1

∴ The value of k is (-1).

questions.question: D, E and F are the feet of the perpendiculars from the vertices A, B and C, respectively, of a triangle ABC. If angle BED and angle BFE (in degrees) are 24 and 110, respectively, what is the measure (in degrees) of angle EBF?
questions.solution:
Given: 

D, E, and F are the feet of the perpendiculars from the vertices A, B, and C, respectively, of a triangle ABC.

∠BED and ∠BFE (in degrees) are 24 and 110

Concept used:

The angle subtended by a chord of a circle at its centre is equal to the angle subtended by the corresponding (minor) arc at the centre.

The sum of all angles in a triangle is always 180°

Calculation:

**Here we have to do construction:**

Draw a circle of diameter AB which passes through D as ∠ADB = 90° 

Draw another circle of diameter BC which passes through E as ∠BEC = 90° 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/31eb89591352567b2434f0be26f65e87c56163158579f428dea0c14319c53bcd.png] 

Taking BC as the diameter, we draw a circle. 

Here, ∠BEC is a subtended angle on circumference from the diameter which is 90°.

Now, considering EC a chord, ∠EBC = ∠EFC = 20°

Now, taking AB as the diameter, we draw a circle.

Here, ∠AEB is a subtended angle on circumference from the diameter which is 90°.

Now, considering BD a chord, ∠BED = ∠BAD = 24°

So, in ΔABD,

∠BAD + ∠ADB + ∠ABD = 180°

⇒ 24° + 90° + ∠ABE + ∠EBD = 180°

⇒ 24° + 90° + ∠ABE + 20° = 180°

⇒ ∠ABE = 46°

⇒ ∠EBF = 46°

**∴ The measure of ∠EBF is 46°.**

questions.question: The average weight of 3 persons A, B and C is 60 kg. When D joins the group, the average weight becomes 65 kg. When another person E whose weight is 3 kg less than that of D replaces A, the average weight of B, C, D and E becomes 67 kg. What is the weight of A?
questions.solution:
Given:

The average weight of 3 persons A, B, and C is 60 kg. 

When D joins the group, the average weight becomes 65 kg. 

E whose weight is 3 kg less than that of D replaces A, the average weight of B, C, D, and E becomes 67 kg.

Concept used:

Total = Average × Number of entities

Calculation:

So, the weight of D = (65 × 4) - (60 × 3) = 80kg

Then, the weight of E = 80 - 3 = 77kg

According to the question,

77 + (60 × 3 - A) + 80 = 67 × 4

⇒ A = 69

**∴ The weight of A is 69kg.**

∠OBA = 42°

Concept used:

The sum of all angles of a triangle is 180°.

questions.question: A pair of jeans marked at Rs. 960 is offered in a departmental store for Rs. 816. What is the percentage of discount given by the shopkeeper?
questions.solution:
Given:

A pair of jeans marked at Rs. 960 is offered in a departmental store for Rs. 816.

Concept used:

Discount = Marked Price - Selling Price

Calculation:

Discount given = (960 - 816) = 144

So, discount % = 144/960 × 100% = 15%

**∴ The percentage of discount given by the shopkeeper is 15%.**

A soft drink company prepares drinks of three different flavours - A, B, C. The production of the three flavours over a period of five years from 2010 to 2014 has been expressed in the given bar graph. Study the graph and answer the question that follows.

Production of three different flavours A, B and C (in lakh bottles) by a company over five years.

The difference between the average production of flavour A in 2012, 2013 and 2014 and the average production of flavour C in 2012, 2013 and 2014 is:
questions.solution:
The average production of flavour A in 2012, 2013 and 2014 = (50 + 45 + 75) ÷ 3 = (170/3) lakh bottles

The average production of flavour C in 2012, 2013 and 2014 = (65 + 70 + 80) ÷ 3 = (215/3) lakh bottles

So, the difference = (215 - 170)/3 = 15 lakh bottles

questions.solution:

x - y = 4 

xy = 3

Concept used:

x³ - y³ = (x - y) (x² + xy + y²)

Calculation:

x - y = 4

⇒ x2 + xy + y2 = 16 + (3 × 3)

⇒ x2 + xy + y2 = 25

⇒ (x - y) (x2 + xy + y2) = 25 × 4

⇒ (x - y) (x2 + xy + y2) = 100

⇒ x³ - y³ = 100

**∴ The value of x3 - y3 is 100.**

questions.question: In a rectangular park having dimensions 60 m × 40 m, two circular flower beds with radius 7 m are developed. What is the area of the remaining portion of the park? (use pi =(22)/(7))
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total area of the park = 60 × 40 = 2400 m²

Area of two flower beds = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × 7 = 308 m²

Remaining area = 2400 − 308 = 2092 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 2092 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the park (L) = 60 m

Breadth of the park (B) = 40 m

Radius of each flower bed (r) = 7 m

**Formula Used:**

Area of rectangle = Length × Breadth

Area of circle = πr²

Remaining Area = Total Area − (2 × Area of circular bed)

 60 m 40 m r = 7 m r = 7 m Remaining Area = Park − 2 × Circle 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of rectangular park = 60 × 40 = 2400 m²

⇒ Area of one circular flower bed = (22/7) × 7 × 7

⇒ Area of one circular flower bed = 22 × 7 = 154 m²

⇒ Total area of two circular beds = 2 × 154 = 308 m²

⇒ Area of remaining portion = 2400 − 308 = 2092 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 2092 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area and Perimeter of a Rectangle

Area = Length × Breadth and Perimeter = 2 × (Length + Breadth).

Area and Circumference of a Circle

Area = πr² and Circumference = 2πr, where r is the radius.

Diagonal of a Rectangle

Diagonal = √(L² + B²), derived from the Pythagoras theorem.
